fullscreen-sheet.purpose: Run a focused mobile task in a near-fullscreen sheet while preserving route context, recovery, validation, and a clear close path.
useWhen: A mobile system needs more than one short action but should not become a new page.
Users need to edit or review contextual data without losing their place.
The task needs step progress, validation, and submit feedback.
doNotUseWithoutReview: The task is permanent navigation or a full screen destination.
The sheet hides critical context needed to make the decision.
Close, back, validation, or focus recovery rules are unclear.
foundations: Defines safe area, sheet edge, internal scrolling, action rail, and responsive density.
Owns title, helper copy, validation, close, back, and submit labels.
Controls action priority, focus, invalid, disabled, and success states.
Separates the sheet from the current route only when it leaves document system.
Uses sheet reveal, step transition, and reduced-motion fallback.
Requires labelled surface, focus containment, Escape/back close, and restored focus.
slots: Opens the mobile task after user intent.
Owns the mobile container and close recovery.
Shows task position for multi-step work.
Back, continue, submit, and cancel actions.
variants: One sheet with one submit step.
Step progress, back/continue, validation, and submit.
Final step summarizes values before submit.
motion: Sheet enters after trigger with Design System reveal timing.
Content changes only after explicit continue/back.
Cancel or submit restores focus to the trigger.
accessibility: The sheet has an accessible title.
Open state starts closed and only changes after user action.
Back and close paths are keyboard reachable.
Focus returns to the trigger after close.
tests: Trigger opens sheet from closed state.
Continue advances only when required data is present.
Back returns to the previous step.
Submit shows feedback and closes the sheet.
Phone viewport keeps actions visible without overlap.

canDecide: Use Fullscreen Sheet for contextual mobile tasks that are larger than an Action Sheet.
Use Stepper when the task has clear ordered steps.
Use Inline Validation for blocked progress.
mustAsk: Navigation ownership, close recovery, destructive submit, or persistence rules are unclear.
rejectIf: The task has no close or back path.
miel.handoff: Confirm trigger, step model, required fields, close behavior, submit consequence, and feedback.
